## Hacktoberfest 2026 × GDG Cloud Nagpur

### A Month of Open Source, Collaboration & Contribution

This October, **GDG Cloud Nagpur** is bringing developers, students, and technology enthusiasts together to celebrate **Hacktoberfest 2026** and explore the world of Open Source.

Whether you are making your **first contribution** or already have experience contributing to open-source projects, this is an opportunity to learn by doing, collaborate with other developers, and make meaningful contributions to real projects.

### What You’ll Experience

* Learn how Open Source and Hacktoberfest work
* Understand Git and GitHub contribution workflows
* Find and work on beginner-friendly open-source issues
* Make your first Pull Request with hands-on guidance
* Get mentorship from experienced contributors
* Learn how to contribute effectively to open-source projects
* Connect and collaborate with fellow developers
* Participate in Hacktoberfest activities throughout October

### Who Should Join?

This event is open to:

* Students
* Developers
* Working professionals
* Open-source beginners
* Experienced contributors
* Anyone interested in learning and contributing to Open Source

**No prior open-source contribution experience is required.**

### Only 50 Participants

To keep the experience **hands-on and mentorship-focused**, we are **hand-picking only 50 participants** for this event.

This means participation is limited, and registration **does not automatically guarantee a spot**.

We will select participants based on their interest in Open Source, willingness to learn, and commitment to actively participate in the session.

### Come Ready to Contribute

Bring your **laptop, curiosity, and willingness to learn**.

Whether you're opening your first Pull Request or looking to deepen your open-source journey, this is your chance to learn, contribute, collaborate, and build alongside the community.

**Learn. Contribute. Build. Repeat.**

— **Team GDG Cloud Nagpur**

maharashtra.name: Hacktoberfest Hack Day Mumbai
maharashtra.description:
​AI belongs to everyone. This October, Hacktoberfest enters a bold new chapter. The days of chasing arbitrary pull-request counts are in the past; this year, we’re coming together for a high-impact, in-person Hack Day focused on hands-on building, experimenting, and shipping with open-source AI and open-weight models.
​Organized by Hackerspace Mumbai in collaboration with our Ecosystem Partner, Paytm, this one-day fest gathers Mumbai’s developers, students, researchers, and builders to explore the frontier of open AI tooling.
​What We’re Hacking On
​Instead of small PR tweaks, this Hack Day is all about practical, builder-first collaboration:
​Open-Source AI Agents: Orchestrating multi-agent systems, autonomous workflows, and agent evaluation.
​Open-Weight & Local Models: Running, benchmarking, and fine-tuning models locally using Ollama, vLLM, and Hugging Face.
​Modern Developer Protocols: Implementing tool-use, skills.md, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and secure agent identities.
​Full-Stack AI Apps: Building practical RAG pipelines and integrating open AI models into everyday web, mobile, and backend apps.
​Who Should Attend?
​Whether you run models on dedicated local GPUs or call APIs from lightweight notebooks, there is a table for you:
​Solo Hackers & Project Leads: Bring an open-source repo, prototype an agentic idea, or build out an open-weight tool.
​Collaborators & First-Time AI Builders: Team up with other builders on sprint challenges, scaffold tools, and learn modern open-source AI workflows hands-on.
​Mentors & Maintainers: Facilitate project tables, guide peers through model runtimes, and review architectures.

neighboring.name: Hacktoberfest Meetup Bengaluru x FailproofAI
neighboring.description:
Our event is a technical roundtable on open source solutions for running AI workers reliably in production. AI workers (autonomous agents that call tools, run long tasks, and act on real systems) are moving from demos into production, and the infrastructure to run them dependably is still being worked out in the open. The roundtable brings practitioners together to map that stack and the OSS projects filling each layer.

We will run it in three parts:

Framing (about 15 minutes): a short setup of what a reliable AI worker stack needs, covering orchestration, observability and tracing, guardrails and policy enforcement, durability and retries, and evaluation.

Roundtable (60 to 75 minutes): a facilitated discussion where practitioners compare the open source tools they use at each layer, where the gaps are, and what is worth building. It is led by people who work on agent reliability infrastructure day to day.

Hacktoberfest contribution (45 minutes): attendees pick relevant OSS projects, triage good first issues together, and open pull requests on the spot, with experienced contributors helping newcomers land their first merged PR.

Everyone leaves with a clearer map of the open source AI infrastructure landscape and at least one contribution in progress.

neighboring.name: Hacktoberfest Hack Day Surat
neighboring.description:
Welcome to Hacktoberfest Hack Day Surat 2026! 🚀

Join us for an official in-person mini-hackathon held at D2 Seminar Hall (Room 207), CK Pithawala College of Engineering and Technology (CKPCET), supported by Major League Hacking (MLH) and DigitalOcean.

Whether you are a seasoned open-source contributor or a beginner exploring AI, this Hack Day is an energetic building sprint focused on open-source tools, collaborative development, and shipping real projects.

---

### 👥 How Team Registration Works:
* **Strictly Individual Registrations:** MLH requires every participant to have their own individual ticket for check-in verification, safety waivers, and swag accounting.
* **Forming Your Squad:** Have each of your teammates (solo or teams of 2–4) register using their own email. 
* **Team Finalization:** You will sit together and register your official team name during the on-site check-in session on October 3.

---

### 🎯 Hackathon Tracks & Themes:
Rather than a rigid single problem statement, this is an open-track sprint. Teams can build any prototype fitting under one of these 3 tracks:
1. **Open-Source AI & Autonomous Agents (Main Track):** Build smart tools, assistants, or autonomous agents using open-weight models (like Google Gemma) or AI APIs.
2. **Developer Tooling & Workflows:** Build practical utilities, CLIs, Git integrations, or developer productivity tools.
3. **Campus & Social Good:** Build solutions addressing student workflow, campus navigation, or community challenges.

---

### 📊 Do You Need a PPT?
* **No pitch decks or PPTs required.**
* Hackathons are about shipping working software. Judging is based on a **2-minute live demo of your working code** on the projector, paired with a public GitHub repository created during the event.

---

### 💻 What to Bring:
* **Your Laptop & Charger (BYOD):** This is strictly a Bring-Your-Own-Device event.
* **Active GitHub Account:** To create and push your project repository.
* **Extension Board (Optional but recommended):** We provide main power strips, but having a compact 2–3 socket extension in your bag is always helpful.

---

### 🎁 Hardware Prizes & Swag:
* **Top 4 Winning Teams:** Arduino Uno Q (4GB) Hardware Development Boards!
* **Runner-Up Tracks:** Official MLH DEV Swag Kits.
* **All Attendees:** Official Google Gemini, Hacktoberfest, DEV, and MLH stickers , plus refreshments & snacks.

*Note: Registrations are strictly capped at 80 seats to maintain a comfortable hacking space. Once full, the registration page will close automatically.*
